newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cultus shares soar on Cornea results.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cultus shares soar on Cornea results.

text.p: Shares in Cultus Petroleum NL soared on Friday after the company released drill results for its Cornea wells which it said pointed to an oil and gas discovery in the Browse Basin, offshore Western Australia.
Cultus shares were trading 40 cents higher at A$1.85 at midday (0100 GMT) after the release of the results following the expiry of an Australian Stock Exchange reporting waiver.

Cultus said the WA-241-P joint venture was assessing all the available well information. "Cultus Petroleum NL believes the information retrieved this far is positive with respect to an oil/gas discovery. However it has drawn no conclusions as to the extent of the accumulation," it said.
Cultus has a 25 percent stake in the WA-241-P joint venture. Operator Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd, has 50 percent and Chevron Asiatic Ltd has 25 percent.
James Capel Australia Ltd oil and gas analyst Mario Traviati said the wildcat discovery was important in terms of delineating new petroleum provinces in the basin.
"The market is right to be excited about it because Shell and Chevron don't drill small structures," he said.
The Browse Basin is located between the Carnarvon Basin and the Timor Sea region.
Cultus said on December 20 that it regarded the Cornea prospect as having the potential to host reserves of more than 100 million barrels of oil.
Cornea-1 was drilled as a "tight hole" because information from it was to be used for bidding for further blocks in the Browse Basin, Cultus said.
